title: FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of convex components and their convex average; strong convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.admissible, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ for every component.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n) Σ_i f_i(x), with positive integer n.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Replies are exact for every call index and oracle seed. There is no oracle error or sampling noise assumption.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.admissible, ∀ k seed i x, HasGradientAt.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Each query selects an index i and point x and returns the exact gradient ∇f_i(x). One selected component gradient counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible.HasGradientAt; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space with a measurable-space structure; finite dimensionality is not required. Every component has globally L-Lipschitz gradient. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. E, n, L, R, ε and x0 are public; the component functions and minimizer are hidden. Valid parameters satisfy L>0, R≥0 and ε>0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: Params; spec.Public, publicInput, valid and admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a measurable E-valued point, its objective gap is integrable, and its expected gap from a global minimizer is at most ε. No particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[F(output)−F(xstar)]≤ε under the product of algorithm and oracle seed laws, with a fixed oracle budget valid for every seed.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard smooth convex finite-sum component-gradient benchmark with expected objective accuracy, stated in a general real Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Smooth Convex Finite-Sum Minimization

We consider minimizing F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x) on a real Hilbert space E, where n≥1 is an integer and each fi:E→R is differentiable and convex with an L-Lipschitz gradient, for L>0. A given starting point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆ of F. The oracle returns ∇fi(x) at a queried pair (i,x). For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap satisfying EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈EF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, which is equipped with a measurable structure. The algorithm receives E, n, L, R, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component convexity). For every i∈{1,…,n}, x,y∈E, and t∈[0,1], fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y).

Assumption 2 (Component smoothness). Each fi is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and ∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E,i∈{1,…,n}.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Queries may select any component i∈{1,…,n} and any point x∈E, and each call returns its exact component gradient. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable with respect to the given measurable structure on E, its objective gap must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
F=n−1∑i=1nfi on a real Hilbert space E equipped with a measurable structure; n≥1, each fi is convex with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0. A minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, R≥0. One oracle call returns an exact component gradient. Target: measurable output x^ with integrable gap and ∫[F(x^(ω))−F(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, ε>0, where P is the algorithm’s sampling law. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

(6) SVRG++ (Allen-Zhu and Yuan 2016, Thm. 4.1). E=Rd, Ψ=0; m0=⌈LR2/Δ⌉, 0<ε<Δ. O(n[1+log⁡(Δ/ε)]+LR2/ε) (2): Matches known rate when Δ≍LR2. (2): Uses log⁡(1+LR2/ε) instead of 1+log⁡(Δ/ε); can lose when Δ≪LR2. No composite term.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex

open OracleTemplate

noncomputable def objective {n : ℕ} {E : Type*} (f : Fin n → E → ℝ) (x : E) : ℝ :=
  (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, f i x

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  n : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero n]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE Params.nonzero

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Fin p.n → p.E → ℝ
  Query p := Fin p.n × p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.n ∧ 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i)) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (oracle.answer k (0, (i, x)) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x y, ‖oracle.answer k (0, (i, x)) seed - oracle.answer k (0, (i, y)) seed‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective f) Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective f) Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective f (output ω) - objective f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective f (output ω) - objective f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex
